stories.title: Planet Money : NPR
stories.description: Connecticut’s property tax system has been broken for decades and the politicians have failed to fix the problem. So now, they’re trying something new: a citizens assembly. (Citizens assemblies are also old. They go back to Ancient Greece, when lawmakers were chosen not through elections, but through random lotteries.) Today on the show, Connecticut’s citizens assembly. It's like jury duty, but for taxes. About hundred random people from all around Connecticut come together to try to solve the state’s property tax problem. They wrestle with whether they should raise taxes, cut spending, find efficiencies, or a mix of everything. Will this alternative attempt to solve the unsolvable succeed, or will it be politics as usual?It’s a modern case study of what happens when politicians step aside to let citizens decide what’s best. Come along as we talk to the professor who helped put this assembly together, learn from the citizens involved how this experiment changed them, and meet the politician who agreed to take their proposals to the state legislature. Planet Money will be at Kilkenomics Festival 2026. Tickets here.Read: - Our book: Planet Money: A Guide to the Economic Forces That Shape Your Life - Our weekly longform Planet Money newsletter- Our weekly Indicator round-up newsletterFollow: - Instagram- TikTok- YouTube- FacebookSupport public media with NPR+ and enjoy perks for over 25 podcasts like this one. This show’s perks include bonus episodes and sponsor-free listening. Learn more at plus.npr.org.This episode of Planet Money was hosted by Erika Beras and Jeff Guo. It was produced by James Sneed with reporting help from Áine Pennello. It was edited by Jess Jiang, Sierra Juarez is our fact-checker, and Jimmy Keeley & Travis Hagen engineered the show. stories.title: HDAR-CNet: hybrid deep learning based spectrum sensing and resource allocation model for cognitive radio networks
stories.description: Cognitive Radio Networks require accurate spectrum sensing and resource allocation to efficiently utilize dynamically available spectrum for varying traffic conditions. To address the issues, this research proposed the Hybrid Deep Learning Based Spectrum Sensing and Resource Allocation model for Cognitive Radio Networks (HDAR-CNet) model. Initially, the Multi-size Kernel Recurrent Transformer Network (MKR-TNet) is proposed for spectrum sensing that is designed using Multi-size Kernel Attention and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) based feed forward network of the transformer. Then, the resource allocation strategy is employed using the proposed Sinusoidal Swift Flight Optimization based Deep Reinforcement Learning (2SO-DRL) model. In the proposed DRL model reward estimation is employed by considering the throughput, delay, user priority and penalty to achieve QoS-aware spectrum allocation. Here, the sinusoidal chaotic mapping incorporated in the proposed 2SO algorithm to improve the exploration, avoid the premature convergence and enhances global optimal solution acquisition. The experimental analysis of the proposed HDAR-CNet model based on End-to-End Spectrum Utilization Efficiency and Computation Time acquired the values of 98.9% and 5 s respectively. Thus, the proposed model provides the efficient, intelligent and reliable solution for next-generation wireless communication systems and Cognitive Radio Networks.

stories.title: Correlation of optical coherence tomography and histology in a laser-induced mouse retinal injury model
stories.description: Understanding the origins of structural features observed in optical coherence tomography (OCT) is essential for improving interpretation of retinal biomarkers. We have developed a workflow to correlate in vivo OCT and OCT angiography with ex vivo histochemistry in a mouse model of laser-induced retinal injury. Adaptive optics OCT provided high-resolution volumetric imaging of lesions, while retinal tissues were subsequently cleared, stained, and imaged with confocal microscopy. A digital tissue-flattening procedure and a two-stage registration pipeline enabled mapping of confocal volumes to OCT datasets using the deep capillary plexus as a structural landmark. Across multiple lesions and animals, hyper-reflective foci (HRF) on OCT co-localised with IB4-positive structures, although inter-lesion variability in the degree of feature correspondence was observed. This framework provides an approach for validation of OCT features to enhance the biological interpretability of retinal imaging biomarkers.
